0x0043eeda: FLD dword ptr [EAX+0x1D4] is the entire operation. D9 /4 with a 32-bit memory operand loads exactly four bytes and pushes them as a float, so the field is a 4-byte float and not a double or an int reinterpreted.

callers_evidence_note: The briefing lists 13 callers; the live scan found 29 code references. 13 are recorded above and the remaining 16 were not individually inspected and are not characterised.
semantic_contract: The function returns, unchanged and without side effects, the 32-bit float stored at offset +0x1D4 of the receiver, delivered on the x87 stack top rather than in an XMM register. It reads exactly one dword, writes nothing at all, calls nothing, and contains no branch. Two of its callers treat the value as a scalar in the unit interval over a per-object population: one picks the largest value among the receiver's eligible children and normalises it through the receiver's own [+0x218, +0x21C] range, and the other returns 1.0f instead when no child is eligible. That makes the field a normalised weight, but the field is not named by the SDK and no caller reveals what it weights.
classification_rationale: The body is nine instructions with one memory operand, one branch-free path and one constant-free encoding, so its mechanics, ABI including the x87 return register, and field offset are complete and certain. STRONG_SEMANTIC is withheld because the one material element the reconstruction cannot supply is the meaning of the field: +0x1D4 is unnamed in the SDK, and the 'normalised blend weight' reading rests on the arithmetic of a single caller rather than on any statement in the binary. The owning type is additionally a two-offset correspondence rather than a proven identity.
semantic_findings: The return is an x87 float in ST(0). That is not an inference from the decompiler's float10 spelling: the body has exactly one FLD, no store and no arithmetic, and the caller's own fallback at 0x0043f4c6 is FLD1, so both sides of the call agree that the value lives on the x87 stack.
The function is a pure field read. It writes no memory, calls nothing, and has no branch.

The frame is a single PUSH ECX with no SUB ESP, which is why the body is 20 bytes rather than the 25 the same sequence costs with a SUB ESP frame - the same shape appears at 0x004ad450 but with an 8-byte frame because that one has two slots.
The receiver is an editor part: the callers address its children at +0x340/+0x344 and its attribute bitset at +0xDC8, matching the SDK's Editors::EditorRigblock.
Callers use the value comparatively, not as a flag: they select a maximum over children and normalise it, and they substitute 1.0f rather than 0 when there is nothing to ask.
unresolved_questions: What does the float at +0x1D4 represent? The 'normalised blend weight' reading comes from FUN_0043ecb0's arithmetic and is labelled INFERRED; the SDK does not name the field and no string or property reference ties it to a concept.
Is the value guaranteed to lie in [0,1]? The caller clamps it into [+0x218, +0x21C] before normalising, which suggests it may not, but nothing in the getter or its 29 callers establishes a range.

Why is the getter out of line at all? It is nine instructions and would inline; a shipped build that kept it out of line may indicate it is a virtual override, an address taken somewhere, or simply an unoptimised translation unit. The 0 data references argue against the vtable case but do not exclude an address being taken.
The 16 code references that were not disassembled could include a caller that treats the value as something other than a weight.
Is the +0x218/+0x21C clamp range per-object or per-class? It is read from the receiver, so per-object, but what sets it was not established.
runtime_gates: No original-process trace has been captured. The value actually stored at +0x1D4 in the shipping build, and its range, are runtime facts that static analysis cannot supply.
Whether the getter is ever reached through a pointer stored in a table, which would explain its out-of-line form, needs a reference scan beyond the 29 direct calls.

validation.byte_exactness: Not byte-identical and not claimed to be, because the receiver is a pointer parameter rather than a thiscall member and the frame is elided: clang -m32 -O2 emits `flds (%ecx); ret` (3 bytes) against the original's 20-byte PUSH EBP / PUSH ECX / spill / reload / FLD [EAX+0x1D4] / teardown. The displacement 0x1D4 is folded into the struct member, the load is a dword load, and the value is returned in ST(0) exactly as the original does.
